title: Forgetting Is a Kind of Blindness. Remembering Is Sight.
excerpt: The Quran describes the whisperer's opening as failing eyesight: whoever goes 'dim-sighted' toward remembrance (yaʿshu, 43:36) is assigned a companion, and the one who turns from remembrance is raised blind (20:124). Recovery is the same faculty reversed — the God-conscious 'remember, and at once they see' (7:201). And the whisperer's own name, al-Khannās, means 'the one who retreats' — he withdraws the instant God is remembered. The disease and the cure are one dial: how clearly you are seeing God right now.
seo_title: Forgetting as Blindness, Remembering as Sight: The Whisper's One Dial (43:36, 7:201, 114:4)
seo_description: A corpus-verified reading: the Quran frames heedlessness as dimming eyesight (yaʿshu, 43:36; raised blind, 20:124) and recovery as restored sight (tadhakkaru fa-mubsirun, 7:201). Al-Khannās, 'the retreater,' withdraws the moment God is remembered. Dhikr is the switch.
